r.h: Kennesaw State Outlasts Kentucky in 35-27 Thriller
p: Kennesaw State and Kentucky traded blows in a high-octane battle that went down to the wire. Coach Clay’s squad struck first with an early rushing touchdown, but Coach Winders kept Kentucky within striking distance throughout a competitive first half. The teams went into the locker room with the outcome hanging in the balance after a flurry of field goals and scoring drives.

The second half turned chaotic, highlighted by a pivotal interception that briefly shifted momentum. While Kentucky managed to reclaim the lead in the fourth quarter, J. Williams took control for Kennesaw State. Williams proved to be the difference-maker, orchestrating a go-ahead touchdown pass to K. Riley before icing the game with a spectacular 40-yard scoring run. Kentucky’s final drive ended in an interception, sealing the 35-27 victory for the visitors.
r.o: J. Williams led a fourth-quarter surge to propel Kennesaw State past Kentucky in a hard-fought road victory.
r.pp: This explosive fourth-quarter run broke the game open, giving Kennesaw State a ten-point cushion that Kentucky could not overcome.

r.h: Kentucky Defense Suffocates North Carolina in 44-0 Rout
p: Coach Winders and the Kentucky Wildcats put on a defensive clinic in Season 3, Week 10, completely dismantling North Carolina in a 44-0 shutout. The game was defined by a relentless Kentucky secondary that feasted on Tar Heel mistakes, recording seven total interceptions. Sebastian Thompson set the tone early with two picks in the first quarter, while Matthew Ivory provided the offensive spark with a 33-yard touchdown run to open the scoring.

The second quarter belonged to Devin Rutherford, who turned the game into a blowout with a 94-yard interception return for a touchdown. Coach Boss's North Carolina squad struggled to find any rhythm as quarterbacks Emerson Slaughter and Jelani Washington were harassed all afternoon by a Kentucky pass rush that featured sacks from Felix Mast and Mychal McMullin. Rutherford eventually finished the day with three interceptions, including a second pick-six in the third quarter.

Kentucky cruised through the final frames, with Washington finding Matthew Ivory for a 26-yard touchdown pass and Ivory adding a short scoring run in the fourth. Despite a 71-yard Ivory touchdown being called back by a penalty, the Wildcats' dominance was never in question as they secured one of the most lopsided victories of the season.
r.o: Kentucky's secondary recorded seven interceptions, including two pick-sixes by Devin Rutherford, to hand North Carolina a devastating 44-0 shutout loss.
r.pp: Devin Rutherford's 94-yard interception return for a touchdown in the second quarter effectively ended North Carolina's hopes and ignited the Kentucky sideline.

r.h: Liberty Holds Off UCF in Week 12 Thriller
p: Skippa’s Liberty squad defended home turf in a back-and-forth contest against Matt’s UCF Knights. The game started with a flurry of defensive scores, as UCF capitalized on a fumble recovery and a pick-six by Battles to take an early lead. Liberty responded with grit, leaning on Taylor Coleman’s explosive playmaking to keep pace before the halftime break.

The second half belonged to the Flames, who utilized timely field goals and a late touchdown to build a cushion. Despite UCF’s desperate fourth-quarter comeback attempt, the Knights were repeatedly hampered by costly holding penalties. A final drive by J. Haden was ultimately snuffed out by Ashton Whitner’s game-sealing interception, securing a 31-23 victory for Liberty.

r.pp: Whitner’s late fourth-quarter pick ended UCF’s final scoring threat, effectively locking up the win for Liberty in a high-stakes moment.

r.h: Boston College Holds Off Liberty Rally in 35-27 Victory
p: Coach Beech and Boston College established early dominance, racing out to a commanding lead behind a 43-yard rushing touchdown from L. Howard and a disciplined defensive performance. The Eagles stifled Skippa’s Liberty offense throughout the first half, forcing multiple turnovers and building a cushion that proved too large for the Flames to overcome despite a late-game surge.

Dante Carr and the Liberty offense found their rhythm too late, struggling against a relentless pass rush led by C. Stare and J. Blonko. While Carr connected with Kinnard and Evans for late scores—including a successful two-point conversion—the Flames' comeback attempt stalled in the final minutes. Boston College’s defense held firm when it mattered most, securing the win despite a late fumble that gave Liberty a glimmer of hope.

r.h: West Virginia Stuns UCF With Massive Comeback
p: Coach Matt and the UCF Knights came out firing in front of their home crowd during Week 11 of Season 3, dominating the early going behind J. Haden and Parker Elmore. UCF seized control with a flurry of touchdowns in the first half, building a commanding lead while forcing multiple interceptions from the West Virginia offense as the Mountaineers struggled to find any rhythm.

Trailing big, Coach Dayce and West Virginia turned the tide in the second half behind a sensational performance from Michael Hawkins Jr. The Mountaineers engineered a remarkable fourth-quarter comeback, scoring 21 unanswered points to stun the Knights. Tim Pinesilver anchored a ferocious defensive effort with seven tackles and two sacks, shutting down UCF's aerial attack as West Virginia stormed back to secure a thrilling 42-31 victory.
r.o: West Virginia erased a massive deficit by scoring 21 unanswered fourth-quarter points to stun UCF 42-31.
r.pp: Michael Hawkins Jr. powered through the defense for a crucial touchdown run, sparking West Virginia's unforgettable fourth-quarter comeback.
